product.schneider-targetpc7640.summary: The transportable AT that combined a plasma display and hard disk in Schneider's range.
product.schneider-targetpc7640.history: The Target PC, identified as PC7640 in Schneider's manual, brought AT compatibility to a transportable format with an integrated display and hard disk. In May 1988, Computerstore advertised it in Germany for DM 5,998; this is a dealer price, not a confirmed launch list price. That same month, Reinhard Schuster offered it with MS-DOS 3.3 alongside the EuroPC and Tower PC desktops: an alternative for moving a workstation between locations.
product.schneider-targetpc7640.warning: Historical research sheet; no validated BluMach emulation.
product.schneider-targetpc7640.technical: Provenance requires distinguishing boards from the complete computer. The manual shows OKI OM-2 markings; Retro-Computer attributes the design to Ai Electronics. That OEM attribution and equivalence with the Rein 420 SLC still need primary-source comparison.
The manual provides a basis for reconstructing the computer. It lists an 80286-8, 82C201/202, 82A203/204/205, MBL8042-144P keyboard controller, HD146818 RTC and WD37C65 floppy controller.

The display needs features beyond basic CGA. The ATS-0020 board contains a V6366B-F and 32 KB; research by fuz and Michael Karcher describes 640 × 400 through ports 03DDh/03DEh, unlocked with bit 7 of 03DFh.

The preserved files do not represent three numbered versions. There are three distinct 32 KiB contents: 129E1 and 129E2 identify as InterLINK 1.29E, and 130 as 1.30. The owner's dump matches 129E1; hashes checked, without a boot test.
The files still need to be mapped to physical chips. The manual lists two 27128 EPROMs; the dumps are 32 KiB images and do not establish chip order on their own.
BluMach holds a research sheet and documentary evidence. The reviewed code has no dedicated PC7640 model; POST and peripherals have not been validated.

Emulation still requires board and V6366 video modelling and boot validation. The available V6355 does not establish equivalence. An image with clear publication rights and confirmation of BIOS-to-board revision correspondence remain pending. No identified dump of the video board U18 EPROM is available yet.
CPC Amstrad International 5/1988: Computerstore advertisement, p. 27, and Reinhard Schuster advertisement, PDF page 60.
Schneider, Service Manual PC7640, Ident-Nr. 36866: components, boards and schematics; two scans preserved.
fuz and Michael Karcher, Retrocomputing Stack Exchange (2020): physical-machine observations and V6366 programming.
Antikythera and contributors, VzEkC (2020–2022): physical specimens, video and problems with SETUP programs from related computers.
Retro-Computer, PC7640 entry: attribution to Ai Electronics and possible rebrands; used as a lead, not proven equivalence.
Schneider PC7640 package on Internet Archive: manual, media and three BIOS files preserved locally.
BluMach, revision 76ecca74: machine inventory and V6355 device; evidence of code status, not historical hardware.

Contemporary advertising identifies the commercial configuration. The May 1988 advertisement lists 640 KB, an advertised upgrade to 2 MB, a 20 MB disk and MS-DOS 3.3; the owner documents a 720 KB floppy drive.
